# What /assess measures

<!-- Generated by skills/assess/scripts/gen_catalog.py (`make catalog`); do not edit by hand. -->

This page lists every check `/assess` and `/fleet` run, what each one reads, and how it
feeds the maturity model. It is generated from the check manifest
(`skills/assess/checks/core.toml`), the default maturity model
(`skills/assess/levels/default.toml`) and the signal input classes
(`skills/assess/scripts/lib/level_signals.py`), so it changes only when they do. The same
data for machines is [measures.json](../skills/assess/references/measures.json).

Nothing here is a judgement of a team. A gap is the next thing to try, and a check that
could not be read is shown as not measured with its reason: it earns nothing and costs
nothing.

## How evidence is graded

Each signal has an input class: what its producer read. The class fixes a grade. Conditions graded measured or verified count toward a level; conditions graded config_only or declared are listed, not counted.

| Grade | Input classes | Counts toward a level |
|---|---|---|
| `config_only` | `config_text` | no, listed |
| `declared` | `head_text` | no, listed |
| `measured` | `execution_artifact`, `git_history`, `head_structure` | yes |
| `verified` | `ci_executed`, `platform` | yes |

A scan that feeds no maturity-model criterion is `unclassified` until its evidence is classified (#789 step 6).

## Conditions by truth tag

Each condition carries one or more truth tags: the truth it keeps honest. A condition holds when all of its criteria hold, and each criterion's key is `<row>.<n>:<signal>`. A condition with several tags is listed under its first tag and named under the others as shared; it counts once. There are 24 conditions, 2 of them with more than one tag.

| Tag | Conditions | Listed here | Shared |
|---|---|---|---|
| Behaviour (`behaviour`) | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| Contracts (`contracts`) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Docs (`docs`) | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Structure (`structure`) | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| Agent context (`agent_context`) | 6 | 6 | 1 |
| Agent runtime (`agent_runtime`) | 4 | 4 | 1 |
| Governance (`governance`) | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| Supply chain (`supply_chain`) | 1 | 0 | 1 |

### Step gates

The autonomy Steps in order. A Step needs its threshold of met, counted conditions and every gate, whatever the gate's grade; gates accumulate, so each Step keeps the gates below it.

| Step | Name | Threshold | New gates | Gate covers | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Assisted | 0 | - | - | - |
| 2 | Supervised agent PRs | 1 | `instructions` | `layer-0-instructions.1` | `agent_context` |
| 3 | Unattended agent PRs | 3 | `ci_runs_tests` | `layer-5-ci.1` | `behaviour` |
| 4 | Autonomous loops | 5 | `coverage_gate` | `layer-6-coverage.1` | `behaviour` |

### Requires, guard and equality links

- `layer-2-design.2` requires `layer-2-design.1`.
- `layer-3-linters.2` requires `layer-3-linters.1`.
- `layer-4-architecture.2` requires `layer-4-architecture.1`.
- `layer-6-coverage.2` requires `layer-5-ci.1`.
- `guardrails-stated.2` requires `guardrails-stated.1`.
- `agent-consistency.2` requires `agent-consistency.1`.

No condition is guarded yet. No criterion compares two signals yet.

## Scans

Every scan name `assess_signals.py --scans` accepts, in run order.

### `agent_ops`: Agent-operations guardrails

Committed permission allowlists, hooks, sandbox rules and routine definitions.

- Collector: `core.agent_ops`, reading `repo_root`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; no string field kept.
- Used by: row `layer-8-agent-ops`.
- Evidence: `agent_ops.summary.permissions_encoded` config_text (config_only), `agent_ops.summary.hooks_present` config_text (config_only), `agent_ops.summary.routines_present` config_text (config_only).
- Not measured when: it cannot read its input; the block says why.

### `config_drift`: Configuration drift

- Collector: `core.config_drift`, reading `repo_root`.
- Network: yes, GitHub or GitLab.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `config_drift.entries.key` token, `config_drift.entries.live` drop, `config_drift.entries.tracked` drop, `config_drift.reason` drop, `config_drift.snapshots.branch` drop, `config_drift.snapshots.doc` drop, `config_drift.snapshots.kind` token.
- Used by: no row or finding yet.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when:
  - `network`: It reads GitHub or GitLab, which only a full /assess run does. Run /assess on the repository with gh or glab signed in.

### `review_reality`: Review on merged changes

Review and approval shares over the sampled merged changes, read through gh or glab.

- Collector: `core.review_reality`, reading `merged_sample`, `gitlab_note_facts`.
- Network: yes, GitHub or GitLab (with --platform).
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `review_reality.reason` drop.
- Used by: row `layer-7-review`.
- Evidence: `review_reality.reviewed_share` platform (verified), `review_reality.approved_share` platform (verified).
- Not measured when:
  - `network`: A headless run without --platform makes no GitHub or GitLab read. Run fleet or assess_signals.py with --platform, or /assess, with gh or glab signed in.
  - `no_remote`: The repository has no GitHub or GitLab remote, so there are no merged changes to read. Nothing to change if the repository is local only; with a GitHub or GitLab remote, /assess and fleet --platform read its merged changes.

### `delivery`: Delivery figures

- Collector: `core.delivery`, reading `merged_sample`, `review_reality`, `fleet_config`, `gitlab_note_facts`.
- Network: yes, GitHub or GitLab (with --platform).
- Headless: only with --platform; left out otherwise.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `delivery.reason` drop.
- Used by: no row or finding yet.
- Evidence: `unclassified`.
- Not measured when:
  - `platform_only`: The block exists only on the platform: without --platform it is left out. Run the fleet or assess_signals.py with --platform, with gh or glab signed in.

### `coverage_gate`: Coverage gate

Finds coverage thresholds written in CI, task-runner and tool config, each with its file, line and threshold.

- Collector: `core.coverage_gate`, reading `repo_root`, `scope`, `excludes`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `coverage_gate.enforced_basis` token, `coverage_gate.gates.form` drop, `coverage_gate.gates.metric` token, `coverage_gate.gates.tool` token, `coverage_gate.gates.unit` token, `coverage_gate.not_detected` drop, `coverage_gate.unmeasured_reason` token.
- Used by: row `layer-6-coverage`.
- Evidence: `coverage_gate.enforced_meets_minimum` ci_executed (verified).
- Not measured when:
  - `go_rust_gate_form_not_read`: The repository holds a go.mod or Cargo.toml with no coverage gate found for it, and no gate of at least 50 percent for another language (a low Python gate beside go.mod is not unmet): its gate may be a script comparing go tool cover (or a report) to a number, which this scan does not read. Nothing to change if a script gates coverage. To have it measured, set the threshold in go-test-coverage's .testcoverage.yml, cargo tarpaulin --fail-under or cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines.

### `agent_environment`: Agent working environment

Committed agent setup, the check command an instruction file names, lockfiles per manifest and the Layer 5 cap; the CI-duration probe is off in headless runs. A manifest row's note is skipped_library (a library whose ecosystem commits no lock: listed, not counted in manifests_total or unlocked_total) or direct_pins_only (a Gradle version catalog or NuGet central package management with no lock: unlocked).

- Collector: `core.agent_environment`, reading `repo_root`, `instruction_files`, `agent_harness`, `excludes`.

### `ci_checks`: CI runs a test or lint command

Whether a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI line runs a test or lint command, whether one can fail its job on ordinary changes (not masked, not off the ordinary triggers), and whether such a line runs a linter; null when no check is found but a CI file pulls its jobs from elsewhere. Null too when no check is found and the tree tracks a CI file the scan does not parse, when under --platform most sampled merged pull requests carry an external CI check, or when a root Prow OWNERS_ALIASES is the only CI evidence.

- Collector: `core.ci_checks`, reading `repo_root`, `ghsync_root`, `gitlab_merged_ci`, `external_ci`.
- Network: no.
- Headless: reported by headless and fleet runs.
- Counts-only: numbers, booleans and nulls kept; strings by field: `ci_checks.basis` token, `ci_checks.enforced_basis` token, `ci_checks.includes.id` id, `ci_checks.includes.kind` token, `ci_checks.includes.ref_basis` token, `ci_checks.includes.status` token, `ci_checks.lint_basis` token, `ci_checks.merged_config` token, `ci_checks.merged_config_reason` token, `ci_checks.reason` drop.
- Used by: row `layer-3-linters`, row `layer-5-ci`.
- Evidence: `ci_checks.lint_runs` ci_executed (verified), `ci_checks.enforced_check_runs` ci_executed (verified).
- Not measured when:
  - `included_jobs`: A CI file pulls its jobs from a file this checkout does not hold, so the check may live there. Nothing to change: this reads as not measured until the included file can be read. On GitLab, fleet --platform reads the merged configuration through the CI lint API.
  - `merged_config_partial`: GitLab's merged CI configuration was read and runs no check, but it may lack jobs: an include under rules: or a trigger: child pipeline is not expanded by the lint API. Nothing to change: a check in a conditional include or child pipeline is not read, so this stays not measured rather than reading false.
  - `unknown_trigger`: In enforced_basis: an unmasked check sits in a workflow or job whose triggers this reader cannot settle (no on: key, a rules: if: on a custom variable). Nothing to change if it runs on every change; naming push or pull_request, or a merge request rule, lets the scan read it.
  - `script_not_found`: In enforced_basis and lint_basis: the only CI line that would settle the signal runs a committed script (./ci.sh, bash scripts/test.sh, ./scripts/lint.sh) that no tracked file matches, so it is not credited; an earlier step may still create it. Commit the script the CI step runs, or call the test or lint command in its own CI step (pytest, ruff check .), so the scan can read it.
  - `check_target`: No CI line runs the linter (lint_basis) or the check (enforced_basis), but one runs a target whose recipe is not read and may run it: make check or npm test for a linter; make foo, npm run foo or ./scripts/foo.sh for a check. Nothing to change if the target runs the check; calling the test or lint command in its own CI step (make test, pytest, ruff check .) lets the scan read it.
  - `unread_ci_system`: No readable GitHub Actions or GitLab CI line settles the signal, and the tree tracks a CI file of a system this scan does not parse (Jenkins, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Buildkite, LUCI, Prow, Zuul and others; the lib/unread_ci.py docstring lists the paths); unread_ci_files counts them. Nothing to change: the scanner cannot read those systems' configuration, so their checks read as not measured rather than absent.
  - `external_ci`: Under --platform only: no readable CI line settles the signal, and over half of the sampled merged pull requests carry a check run or status of a known external CI system (Buildkite, LUCI, Prow tide, Azure Pipelines). A check ran; that earns no credit. Nothing to change: the checks run on a CI system configured outside the repository, so they read as not measured rather than absent.
  - `external_ci_marker`: The tree tracks no CI file of any kind and the root holds a Prow OWNERS_ALIASES file, so presubmits likely run on Prow, configured in another repository. An OWNERS file alone is not a marker. Nothing to change: run with --platform to read the checks on merged pull requests instead.
  - `analysers_in_build`: In lint_basis: no CI line runs a linter, but a CI dotnet build runs the analysers a committed Directory.Build.props or .csproj turns on (EnforceCodeStyleInBuild, AnalysisLevel). Their severities live in .editorconfig, which the scan does not evaluate. Nothing to change if the analysers fail the build on a finding; a CI step running dotnet format --verify-no-changes lets the scan read a lint run.
  - `compiler_gate_only`: In lint_basis: no CI line runs a linter, and the only static gate is a compiler run with warnings as errors (mix compile --warnings-as-errors, -Werror, dotnet build -warnaserror, TreatWarningsAsErrors in Directory.Build.props). It is not counted as a lint run. Running a linter or analyser in its own CI step (mix credo, clang-tidy, dotnet format --verify-no-changes) lets the scan read a lint run.

  - `invalid_import_graph`: A builder returned a graph that breaks the module-graph contract. Report it against the toolkit; structure reads as not measured meanwhile.
  - `no_source_files`: The scope holds no source file in a language the assess skill recognises. Nothing to change if the scope has no code; check the scope and the excludes otherwise.
